emergency.heading: Gas Safety First — What to Do Right Now

steps.title: Evacuate immediately
steps.text: Get everyone—including pets—out of the house and into fresh air right away if you smell gas.

steps.title: Create zero sparks
steps.text: Do not flip light switches, unplug appliances, open the garage door, or use phones inside.

steps.title: Call 911 and your utility
steps.text: From outside at a safe distance, call 911 and Southwest Gas (or your provider) to secure the meter.

steps.title: Call our licensed plumbers
steps.text: Once the scene is safe or locked out, call us for pressure testing and permanent pipe repair.

phoenixAngle.heading: Why Desert Sun & Alkaline Soil Affect Phoenix Gas Lines
paragraphs: Across Phoenix and the Valley, outdoor gas runs feed pool heaters, patio fire pits, and built-in BBQ islands. Intense UV exposure dries out unprotected pipe coatings and appliance flex hoses, while alkaline desert soil and lawn irrigation moisture can corrode older buried steel piping that lacks proper wrapping or dielectric isolation.

When a utility technician locks a meter for safety, restoring gas quickly requires accurate branch isolation, clean code-compliant repairs, and adherence to local municipal pressure-test inspection rules before the utility returns to unlock your residential gas meter safely for your home.

faqs.q: What should I do first if I suspect a gas leak in my house?
faqs.a: Leave the building immediately without turning lights on or off, using garage door openers, or dialing inside. Once outside at a safe distance, call 911 and your gas utility so they can shut off the meter and make the area safe first.

faqs.q: Can a plumber unlock my gas meter after Southwest Gas shuts it off?
faqs.a: No—only the gas utility unlocks their meter. However, a licensed Arizona plumber must locate the leak, complete the repair, pass a static pressure test, and arrange any required city inspection before the utility returns to restore gas flow safely indoors.

faqs.q: Why did a home inspector flag an old gas flex connector behind my stove?
faqs.a: Older uncoated brass connectors and shutoff valves can crack or seep when an appliance is pulled out for cleaning. Replacing them with modern coated stainless flex lines and quarter-turn rated valves keeps the connection safe, durable, and fully code-compliant indoors.

faqs.q: How do you find a hidden leak in an underground backyard gas line?
faqs.a: We isolate the outdoor branch from the house system, apply a controlled test pressure, and use calibrated electronic gas detectors and soap-bubble checks at risers—or trace the buried line route if excavation is needed to expose a corroded underground section.

faqs.q: Does gas line repair require a city permit in Phoenix?
faqs.a: Rules differ by city and by the specific work being done. Minor valve or appliance connector swaps differ from buried pipe replacements or meter-lockout clearances that require municipal inspection before utility reconnection. Your licensed plumber will explain clearly what applies.

faqs.q: Do you repair propane lines as well as natural gas piping?
faqs.a: Yes. Our licensed plumbers pressure-test and repair both municipal natural gas piping and residential propane systems, matching pressure regulators, rated shutoff valves, sediment traps, and pressure-test standards to your home's specific fuel type and outdoor patio appliances safely today without shortcuts.
